To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified and characterized a new PCP-A promoter from B. rapa ssp chinensis.

the promoter of a PCP-A gene family member, BcMF5, was isolated from B. rapa ssp. chinensis and the promoter activity was confirmed by transient expression analysis in onion cells and stable transformation analysis in Arabidopsis.
the BcMF5 pollen promoter was identified and preliminarily characterized in Brassica rapa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new promoter from B. rapa and the analysis of its expression pattern.
a new pollen promoter from Chinese cabbage-pak- choi, which may be used to study gene function and to improve crop production.
the promoter of BCP-A gene family in Brassica rapa, which is expected to be used for the development of pollen-specific expression vectors in transgenic plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BcMF5 gene promoter is a novel pollen coat protein gene promoter from Brassica species.
this promoter can be used as a pollen-specific promoter in plant genetic transformation.
this study has successfully identified a new PCP gene promoter from Brassica and provided a new tool for the study of the molecular mechanisms of PCP expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BcMF5 is a pollen promoter and the −377 to + 3 bp fragment of its promoter is sufficient for pollen gene expression.
the promoter of Brassica BcMF5 was identified and preliminarily analyzed, and it was demonstrated that BcMF5 could be used as a pollen-specific promoter in Brassica rapa.
the BcMF5 is a novel pollen coat promoter, and the BcMF-5 promoter can drive high level expression of transgenes in the anther and pollen.   1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BcMF5, a PCP-A gene, is a pollen-specific gene, which is expressed at different stages of anther development.

BcMF5 is the first promoter from Brassica that has been characterized as a pollen promoter, and that the promoter of the BcMF5 gene may be a useful tool for the genetic engineering of male sterility in Brassica.
the promoter of the PCP-A gene from B. rapa is active in pollen development and that it can drive high levels of gene expression in anther and flower development.
